limitations: Small development-mode local synthetic smoke; not a production benchmark, memory-leak test, or Cloudflare measurement.
Phase1 already uses Next16/React19; comparison is of the later UI/Virtual dependency batch as a whole.
The page includes hidden reference120, development framework code and Clerk/CDN work. Heap and longtask entries cannot isolate application-only resource use or a package-specific effect.
Runtime.getHeapUsage measures approximate JavaScript heap for the CDP page target/isolate, not total browser RAM, all frame heaps, GPU memory, or all DOM/Blink allocations.
Garbage collection is forced by the harness at the same checkpoints. It changes execution timing; these timings do not replace the separate three-run performance evidence.

PerformanceObserver longtask captures tasks at least50ms and browsing-context attribution, not source-function or library attribution. Stage assignment uses task start time and is approximate for work spanning stages.

The fresh contexts, main-page telemetry and observer/harness objects also contribute to these values. Two samples do not support improvement percentages or conclusions about retained memory over long sessions.
Chromium headless desktop viewport only; physical iOS, momentum scrolling, and production auth/network workloads remain outside this smoke.

Both origins lack /favicon.ico. The first sample per origin logged one generic404; separate navigation diagnostics identify favicon404, with no unhandled page exceptions or development error overlay. Raw console observations remain preserved.
